prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” HVAC company that fits every situation — the right contractor depends on your location, the exact problem, your budget, whether you need emergency service, and whether your system is under warranty. I can help you find the best option for your case. A few quick questions first:

- What’s your ZIP code or neighborhood in Phoenix?
- What’s the problem with the AC (not cooling, short-cycling, leaking water, noisy, no fan, ice on coils, etc.)?
- How old is the system / do you know the make and model?
- Is this an emergency (no cooling in extreme heat)?

If you want to start immediately, here are practical next steps and how to choose a reliable company:

Immediate troubleshooting (safe, quick checks)
- Check the thermostat (set to cool, temperature lower than room, batteries if digital).
- Check AC circuit breaker in the electrical panel; reset if tripped.
- Replace or inspect the air filter — a clogged filter can stop cooling.
- Make sure outdoor unit is clear of debris and has good airflow.
- If the outdoor fan isn’t running or you smell burning, power off and call a pro.

How to pick a good Phoenix HVAC contractor
- License: Verify the contractor is licensed by the Arizona Registrar of Contractors (ROC) for HVAC work.
- EPA 608 certification: Required for refrigerant handling.
- Insurance: Ask for proof of liability insurance and worker’s comp.
- Reviews & reputation: Check Google, Yelp, BBB, Angi, and local Facebook groups.
- Experience with your system: Ask if they service your AC brand/model.
- Clear pricing: Get a written estimate that lists parts, labor, permits, and diagnostics fee.
- Warranty: Ask about workmanship guarantees and parts warranties.
- Availability: If it’s an emergency, check who offers 24/7 or same-day service.

What I can do for you now
- Find and list top-rated HVAC contractors in your Phoenix ZIP with ratings and links.
- Draft an email or phone script you can use to get comparable quotes.
- Help interpret estimates and warranty terms.

Tell me your ZIP and the problem, and I’ll pull together a short list of reputable local companies and what to ask each.
